name: Automate
description: Automations for agents: reminders, schedules, webhooks and event triggers that create tasks, message a channel or start a flow. Same engine as the Automate window.

-health-check.name: -health-check
-health-check.description: Internal health check. Verifies the connection to the Teros backend.

list-automations.name: list-automations
list-automations.description: List the automations of the workspace: name, trigger (schedule / once / webhook / event), action (create-task / channel-event / start-flow), status, next run and 7-day stats. Filter by trigger, action, status or a name search; paginate with limit + cursor.

params.status: Only active or only disabled automations.
params.timezone: IANA timezone for the human-readable times (default: env).

get-automation.name: get-automation
get-automation.description: Get one automation by id: full trigger and action configuration, resolved target names and stats. Webhook tokens are never returned.

list-executions.name: list-executions
list-executions.description: Execution history of an automation, newest first: what fired it (schedule / once / webhook / event), whether it succeeded, the task or flow run it produced, the error if any. Rows with skipped:true never ran: a guard refused them. error starting with "quota-automate_daily_limit" means the user had used up their plan's Automate runs for that UTC day (see get-quota: explain the limit, the reset at 00:00 UTC, and the ways out — space the schedule out, disable a noisy automation, or upgrade the plan); error starting with "billing-" means their agent-hours or payment blocked it.

get-quota.name: get-quota
get-quota.description: The user's daily Automate budget: how many runs their plan allows per UTC day (all automations and trigger kinds together — schedules, reminders, webhooks and events), how many ran today, how many are left, when it resets (00:00 UTC) and which automations ran most. Use it before creating a frequent schedule, and whenever an automation "did not fire": if used >= limit the runs are being skipped until the reset. Ways out: space the schedule out, disable a noisy automation, or upgrade the plan (Profile → Plan). limit 0 means unlimited.

list-webhook-calls.name: list-webhook-calls
list-webhook-calls.description: Recent payloads received by a webhook automation, newest first (max 50): when, discriminator, whether a task was created or updated, the payload.

list-upcoming.name: list-upcoming
list-upcoming.description: What will fire next: active schedule and once automations ordered by next run, within a window (default 7 days). Optionally only those that message a given channel.

params.channelId: Only automations whose action targets this channel.

list-event-topics.name: list-event-topics
list-event-topics.description: The event catalog of the workspace: every topic the installed apps declare they emit (Telegram messages, board task changes, …) with the payload fields usable in filters and templates, plus templateSyntax — the exact template grammar. Call it before creating an event automation.

params.appId: Only topics of this installed app.
params.search: Substring of the topic or app name.

parse-time-expression.name: parse-time-expression
parse-time-expression.description: Preview a time expression without creating anything. Accepts natural language — recurring ("cada lunes a las 9", "weekdays a las 8", "every 2 hours" → cron + human description) or one-shot ("tomorrow at 9am", "in 2 hours", "mañana a las 9") — ISO 8601, or a 5-field cron. Returns kind (once | cron), the resolved time / cron description and the next occurrences. Use this to tell the user when an automation will run, in plain language.

params.previewCount: How many occurrences to preview (1-10, default 3).
params.reference: ISO reference instant for relative expressions (default now).

create-automation.name: create-automation
create-automation.description: Create an automation: one trigger (schedule, once, webhook or event) coupled with one action (create a task, message a channel, start a flow). Returns the automation and, for webhooks, the secret URL — shown only once. For event triggers it also returns the payload fields of the topic and warns about filters/templates that use fields the event does not carry. Use idempotencyKey to make retries safe.

params.name: Short name shown in the Automate window.
params.trigger: When it fires. {type:"schedule", schedule, timezone?, locale?} (natural language, PRIMARY: "cada lunes a las 9", "weekdays a las 8", "cada 2 horas", "el primer día de mes") | {type:"schedule", cron, timezone?} (advanced: 5-field cron) | {type:"once", at, timezone?, locale?} (natural language or ISO; fires once) | {type:"webhook"} (a secret URL is generated) | {type:"event", topic, filters?} (topic from list-event-topics; filters = array of {field: value} objects, OR-ed).
params.action: What happens. {type:"create-todo-item", parentId?, assignee?, state?, plannedDay?, plannedTime?, textTemplate, descriptionTemplate?, instructionsTemplate?} (creates a task in the to-do list / Tasks tree — parent group optional, assignee {kind:"agent"|"user", id}, plannedDay "YYYY-MM-DD") | {type:"create-task", projectId, agentId?, columnId?, titleTemplate, instructionsTemplate, descriptionTemplate?} (creates a task on a project board) | {type:"channel-event", channelId?, agentId?, messageTemplate} (defaults: current channel and agent) | {type:"start-flow", flowId, projectId, inputMapping?}. Templates: {{field}} / {{payload.field}} / {{topic}} / {{payload}} (JSON) / {{a || b || "literal"}} (first non-empty wins); nothing else ({{#if}} etc. is rejected). Required templates (title/instructions/message/text) must not render empty; the trigger payload becomes the task input artifact.
params.idempotencyKey: Same key twice → the first automation is returned, nothing duplicated.

schedule-reminder.name: schedule-reminder
schedule-reminder.description: Remind at a given time: the message is delivered once to the channel (default: this conversation) and the agent acts on it. time: natural language ("tomorrow at 9am", "in 2 hours", "el lunes a las 10") or ISO 8601.

params.time: Natural language or ISO 8601, in the future.
params.message: What the agent receives when it fires (max 4000 chars).
params.timezone: IANA timezone the time is expressed in (default: env).

create-recurring-task.name: create-recurring-task
create-recurring-task.description: Deliver a message to a channel on a recurring schedule (default channel: this conversation); the agent acts on it each time. schedule: natural language, PRIMARY ("cada lunes a las 9", "weekdays a las 8", "cada 2 horas"); cron: 5 fields "min hour day month weekday" (advanced).

params.schedule: Natural language (PRIMARY): "cada lunes a las 9", "weekdays a las 8", "cada 15 minutos", "el primer día de mes".
params.message: What the agent receives on each run (max 4000 chars).
params.timezone: IANA timezone of the cron (default: env).
params.name: Name in the Automate window (default: the message).

create-webhook.name: create-webhook
create-webhook.description: Create a webhook: a secret URL external systems POST JSON to; each call runs the action (create a task — with discriminator dedupe —, message a channel, or start a flow). The URL is returned once.

params.name: Short name, e.g. "GitHub issues → tasks".
params.action: What happens. {type:"create-todo-item", parentId?, assignee?, state?, plannedDay?, plannedTime?, textTemplate, descriptionTemplate?, instructionsTemplate?} (creates a task in the to-do list / Tasks tree — parent group optional, assignee {kind:"agent"|"user", id}, plannedDay "YYYY-MM-DD") | {type:"create-task", projectId, agentId?, columnId?, titleTemplate, instructionsTemplate, descriptionTemplate?} (creates a task on a project board) | {type:"channel-event", channelId?, agentId?, messageTemplate} (defaults: current channel and agent) | {type:"start-flow", flowId, projectId, inputMapping?}. Templates: {{field}} / {{payload.field}} / {{topic}} / {{payload}} (JSON) / {{a || b || "literal"}} (first non-empty wins); nothing else ({{#if}} etc. is rejected). Required templates (title/instructions/message/text) must not render empty; the trigger payload becomes the task input artifact.

update-automation.name: update-automation
update-automation.description: Change an automation: name, trigger, action and/or enabled. Trigger and action use the same shapes as create-automation and replace the previous ones; runtime state (counters, webhook token) is kept. Switching the trigger to webhook returns a new URL once.

enable-automation.name: enable-automation
enable-automation.description: Enable (resume) an automation. Idempotent. A disabled schedule re-arms at its next cron slot.

disable-automation.name: disable-automation
disable-automation.description: Disable (pause) an automation without deleting it. Idempotent. It keeps its configuration and history.

snooze-reminder.name: snooze-reminder
snooze-reminder.description: Postpone a once automation (reminder) by a delay — "30m", "2h", "1d" — on top of its current time. Re-arms it if it already fired.

regenerate-webhook-url.name: regenerate-webhook-url
regenerate-webhook-url.description: Rotate the secret URL of a webhook automation. The old URL stops working immediately; the new one is returned once.

test-webhook.name: test-webhook
test-webhook.description: Fire a webhook automation with a test payload, exactly as an external POST would (dedupe, audit, stats). The action really runs.

params.payload: JSON object the action receives as {{payload}}.

delete-automation.name: delete-automation
delete-automation.description: Permanently delete an automation. It stops firing immediately; tasks, messages and flow runs it already produced are kept. Irreversible.

cancel-reminder.name: cancel-reminder
cancel-reminder.description: Cancel a pending reminder (once automation). Idempotent: an already fired or missing reminder returns noop.

bulk-cancel.name: bulk-cancel
bulk-cancel.description: Delete several automations at once: by ids, or every automation that targets a channel, optionally only a trigger kind and only those whose next run is before an ISO date. Max 100 per call. Irreversible.

params.channelId: Every automation whose action targets this channel.
params.before: ISO date: only automations whose next run is before it.

changelog.1.0.0: Initial release — automations (schedule / once / webhook / event × create-task / channel-event / start-flow) over the backend automate.* API; absorbs the scheduler MCA (reminders, recurring tasks, snooze, bulk cancel, upcoming, time parsing).
